maya: quick check — is the orders index created CONCURRENTLY? we can't block the orders table during peak test traffic.

deploy-bot: Migration 20250320_add_orders_index started (pid=4821)
```sql
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_customer_id ON orders (customer_id);
```
(note: migration runner did not include CONCURRENTLY)

infra-bot: Observability alert: long-running exclusive lock on table "orders" detected for pid=4821 (+90s). Query: CREATE INDEX idx_orders_customer_id ON orders (customer_id)

jack: whoa — that's going to block writes. @eli can you abort and re-run with CONCURRENTLY? if not, we should pause the deploy.

eli: aborting migration pid=4821 now. running: `pg_cancel_backend(4821)` -> cancelled (signal sent).

deploy-bot: Migration 20250320_add_orders_index aborted by @eli (reason: exclusive lock).

eli: spinning up safe alternative: applying `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_orders_customer_id ON orders (customer_id);` starting now. This will avoid long-held locks but may take longer overall. Running in background.

deploy-bot: Started migration 20250320_add_orders_index_concurrent (pid=4890).

maya: thanks. also confirm backfill will be batched (10k rows) and rate-limited. we don't want to overwhelm replicas.

deploy-bot: 20250320_backfill_order_status started (job_id=bf-77). Backfill strategy: batch_size=10000, pause_ms=200 between batches. Estimated completion: ~4m.

infra-bot: Replica lag spike observed ~35s during non-concurrent attempt — now stabilizing since concurrent run started.

eli: monitoring backfill and concurrent index. so far index progress: 22% (scanning pages). backfill: processed 2/40 batches.

jack: preference: continue deploy to staging. if concurrent index or backfill fails, we will abort and roll back to previous tag. call it here if needed.
